purpose: Pictologics is a 3D Slicer extension for researchers to extract IBSI-compliant radiomic features (intensity, morphology, and texture) from 3D scalar volumes and segmentations across single cases or study batches. It provides presets, an in-app preprocessing and filter-bank builder, provenance tracking, a read-only results browser, and full-precision CSV/JSON export.
summary:
Pictologics is a remarkably well-engineered radiomics extension for 3D Slicer. It meets all three admission requirements: (1) safety and environment isolation are exemplary, installing pinned wheel-only dependencies into an extension-private directory only after explicit user consent and running all computations in an isolated subprocess without mutating Slicer's shared Python packages; (2) licensing is clear under Apache-2.0 with proper `NOTICE` and dataset attributions; and (3) the catalog entry and CMake build configuration are complete and consistent.

🟢 Recommend merge

safety.rationale: Inspected all runtime Python modules (`PictologicsSlicer.py`, `PictologicsCLI.py`, `PictologicsLib/*.py`, `PictologicsWidgets/*.py`) and searched the repository for network, subprocess, and deserialization calls. There is no telemetry, no unauthorized network transmission, no unsafe deserialization (`yaml.safe_load` and strict JSON are used), CSV exports guard against formula injection (`spreadsheet_safe`), exported provenance redacts the user's home directory, and diagnostics use strict allowlists.

environment.rationale: Inspected `PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsSlicer.py`, `PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsLib/dependencies.py`, `PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsLib/dependency_probe.py`, and `PictologicsCLI/PictologicsCLI.py`. The extension never installs or imports `pictologics` into Slicer's shared Python environment; instead, after explicit user confirmation (`confirmOkCancelDisplay`), it installs wheel-only pinned dependencies into an extension-private `--target` folder under `AppLocalDataLocation` and runs all computations in a separate `PythonSlicer` CLI subprocess with shared `site-packages` stripped from `sys.path`.

packaging.rationale: Inspected `Pictologics.json`, root `CMakeLists.txt`, `PictologicsSlicer/CMakeLists.txt`, and `PictologicsCLI/CMakeLists.txt`. All Python modules, widgets, UI files, icons, and requirements/constraints files imported by the extension are listed in CMake and exist in the repository, and `build_dependencies: []` matches `EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA"`.

license.rationale: Inspected `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `README.md`, and `docs/screenshots/README.md`. The repository is clearly licensed under the permissive Apache License 2.0, with proper attribution in `NOTICE` and `CC BY-SA 4.0` attribution for the Medical Segmentation Decathlon `CTLiver` sample used in documentation screenshots.

soundness.rationale: Inspected `PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsSlicer.py`, `PictologicsCLI/PictologicsCLI.py`, and `PictologicsSlicer/PictologicsLib/*.py`. The extension is exceptionally well-engineered: heavy work runs asynchronously in a cancellable CLI worker, scene lifecycle and observer cleanup are carefully managed, atomic file writes and rollback guards protect user data, and IEEE 754 float64 table values are preserved across MRB scene saves.

utility.rationale: Inspected `README.md`, `docs/*.md`, `PictologicsSlicer/Testing/`, `PictologicsCLI/Testing/`, and `tests/`. The extension provides comprehensive user and developer documentation, clear research-use-only disclaimers, full preprocessing and software provenance alongside feature exports, and an extensive unit and integration test suite.

findings.title: Multiple large derivative branding assets committed to the source repository
findings.evidence:
assets/branding/pictologics/raster/pictologics-master-1254.png  (1675535 bytes, binary)
assets/branding/pictologics/raster/pictologics-master-1254.webp  (1144018 bytes, binary)
assets/branding/pictologics/raster/pictologics-vector-render-4096.png  (1223228 bytes, binary)
assets/branding/pictologics/raster/pictologics-white-1254.jpg  (597284 bytes, binary)
findings.explanation: The repository includes 22 derivative branding files in `assets/branding/pictologics/` (including a ~2 MB `.icns`, ~2 MB `.tiff`, ~1.7 MB master PNG, ~1.2 MB 4096px PNG, ~1.1 MB `.eps`, ~1.1 MB `.webp`, ~1.1 MB 1024px PNG, and ~0.9 MB `.svg`), totaling ~13 MB in the git checkout. While CMake properly excludes these from the built Slicer extension archive, committing multiple multi-megabyte master and print-format derivatives increases repository clone size for the Extensions Index build system and contributors.
findings.suggestion: Consider keeping only the catalog/module PNG icons and the master source (or generating derivatives on demand with `scripts/export_branding_assets.py`) to keep the git repository lightweight.
